posts.name: TeslaRoyale
posts.cooked:
Each Sentinel counts as a hero character card but they collectively only count as 1h. They still follow the normal rules in terms of play power and draw. The character cards all count as cards in play. Anything that targets the player hits all of them. Anything that targets a hero or hero target hits one of them. Cards like infection have their own rules detailed in the rule book.

Yes, there are ongoings and oneshots in the decks. The primary difference is in how they set up which is one villian then one hero and so on and so forth until the enviornment.

Does that help?

posts.name: pwatson1974
posts.cooked:
Each Vengeance deck has their own one shots and ongoings that mostly just affect themselves (Baron Blade and Friction have cards that autoplay other villan decks but it doesn't matter much which decks are around). They don't depend on specific decks being in play.

 

The Sentinels have a card that lets them use a power when they deal damage, so you can get two powers out of them a round. The Sentiels are one hero and 4 hero targets. If the Sentiels can't use powers, none of them can. However, if a target damages the hero, raher than hero target, I say it only hits one of them. However, this was never confirmed during the plytesting so may be resolved differently.

Iron Legacy can actually get a perfect set-up that can incap all The Sentinels on the very first turn! But it's not all bad, at least they have Ongoing destruction on their incap!

They each have a signature card that only applies when that particular member is still active.

Idealist tend to be targeted for the lowest target quite often, but they have great healing.

If the Ensnaring Brambles made it where the lowest hero target could not deal damage, and if Idealist is the lowest, then she would not be able to deal damage. The other three would however continue to be able to deal damage.

Most cards list the individuals. A lot of One-shots even have two members do two different things. There is Sentinels Tactics, which will trigger if any member of the Sentinels deals damage.

No, they don't have individual incaps.  The setup card has their incaps, and it isn't flipped over until all 4 are incapped.  They do, however, have a choice of 4 incap abilities instead of the usual 3.

 

They have a one-shot that allows Medico to un-incap any other Sentinel, and they have another that lets you un-incap any one Sentinel (in case Medico gets incapped).  I forget how many copies of each, but it's something like x3 and x2 respectively.
